text:
The tail device M5 is the most likely corrupted element. It is the only device whose operating point is clearly anomalous. Its drain is at 58 mV, below its 178 mV Vdsat, so it is in triode. That makes its current set by Vds rather than by the M6 mirror. M5 carries 5.13 uA, while the M5/M6 ratio of 1.163 should give about 11.6 uA in saturation. The diff pair's tail current is therefore starved, which lowers loop gain and damping. This matches the failing ripple_settled metric and the largest ripple sensitivity to M5. M2 is second because it has the largest sensitivity and sets the tail node voltage. M6 is third because it sets the mirror reference that M5 should follow.

{"ranking": ["M5", "M2", "M6"], "fault": "Tail current mirror device M5 has a wrong size (mirror ratio to M6 too small, about 1.16 instead of the intended value), so M5 carries about 5 uA instead of its mirrored current and is pushed into triode (Vds 58 mV < Vdsat 178 mV). This starves the diff pair, reducing gm and loop damping, which causes the residual ringing (ripple_settled 0.017 V vs 0.01 V limit)."}
